## Your budget

You have 5 minutes and 40 tool calls for this task. A grep costs about 5
seconds, a test run can cost 30. Call get_status to see what remains.

Spend at most a third of your budget locating the code. Once you have a
plausible diagnosis, edit the source — a wrong patch scores the same as no
patch, so an unverified fix always beats an unfinished investigation. If
get_status shows half your time gone and you have not yet edited a source
file, stop investigating and make your best edit now.

## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Edit the source first. Only write a reproduction script once you have made
your edit and submitted it, and only if budget remains to run it.

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — everything left
in /workspace becomes your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py or
pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

The harness truncates what you receive: 5,000 characters from any command,
and 150 lines or 10,000 characters from read_file. A truncated result loses
information silently, so a broad read wastes a call AND leaves you guessing.

Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Then read_file with a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole
file and never cat one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

def _iter_syntax_lines(
    start: SyntaxPosition, end: SyntaxPosition
) -> Iterable[Tuple[int, int, int]]:
    """Yield start and end positions per line.

    Args:
        start: Start position.
        end: End position.

    Returns:
        Iterable of (LINE, COLUMN1, COLUMN2).
    """

    line1, column1 = start
    line2, column2 = end

    if line1 == line2:
        yield line1, column1, column2
    else:
        for first, last, line_no in loop_first_last(range(line1, line2 + 1)):
            if first:
                yield line_no, column1, -1
            elif last:
                yield line_no, 0, column2
            else:
                yield line_no, 0, -1

    def ipy_excepthook_closure(ip: Any) -> None:  # pragma: no cover
        tb_data = {}  # store information about showtraceback call
        default_showtraceback = ip.showtraceback  # keep reference of default traceback

        def ipy_show_traceback(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
            """wrap the default ip.showtraceback to store info for ip._showtraceback"""
            nonlocal tb_data
            tb_data = kwargs
            default_showtraceback(*args, **kwargs)

        def ipy_display_traceback(
            *args: Any, is_syntax: bool = False, **kwargs: Any
        ) -> None:
            """Internally called traceback from ip._showtraceback"""
            nonlocal tb_data
            exc_tuple = ip._get_exc_info()

            # do not display trace on syntax error
            tb: Optional[TracebackType] = None if is_syntax else exc_tuple[2]

            # determine correct tb_offset
            compiled = tb_data.get("running_compiled_code", False)
            tb_offset = tb_data.get("tb_offset", 1 if compiled else 0)
            # remove ipython internal frames from trace with tb_offset
            for _ in range(tb_offset):
                if tb is None:
                    break
                tb = tb.tb_next

            excepthook(exc_tuple[0], exc_tuple[1], tb)
            tb_data = {}  # clear data upon usage

        # replace _showtraceback instead of showtraceback to allow ipython features such as debugging to work
        # this is also what the ipython docs recommends to modify when subclassing InteractiveShell
        ip._showtraceback = ipy_display_traceback
        # add wrapper to capture tb_data
        ip.showtraceback = ipy_show_traceback
        ip.showsyntaxerror = lambda *args, **kwargs: ipy_display_traceback(
            *args, is_syntax=True, **kwargs
        )

    try:  # pragma: no cover
        # if within ipython, use customized traceback
        ip = get_ipython()  # type: ignore[name-defined]
        ipy_excepthook_closure(ip)
        return sys.excepthook
    except Exception:
        # otherwise use default system hook
        old_excepthook = sys.excepthook
        sys.excepthook = excepthook
        return old_excepthook
